summary: A 1970 list of the Network Working Group notes numbered 1 to 80, compiled by J. B. North. It is an index.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 84 is a catalog of Network Working Group notes numbered 1 through 80. Its entries give dates, NIC numbers, titles and authors, and it marks some numbers as never issued.

subtitle: An index listing Network Working Group RFCs numbered 1 through 80.

tldr.problem: Readers needed a way to identify and locate earlier Network Working Group notes.
tldr.mechanism: J. B. North lists entries for NWG/RFCs 1 through 80 with dates, NIC numbers, titles and authors, including entries marked never issued.
tldr.outcome: The document serves as a catalog of early network notes rather than a technical specification.

today: The unit metadata records RFC 84 as Unknown and lists no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It is an index of Network Working Group RFCs 1 through 80, dated 23 December 1970.

sections.title: What the Catalog Lists
sections.content:
J. B. North's list covers NWG/RFC numbers 1 through 80. For each listed note, it gives a date, a NIC number, a title and an author or authors.

The document includes entries that say a number was never issued, as well as entries for issued notes.
sections.plainLanguage: The catalog helps readers identify early network notes by number, title, date and author. It also identifies some numbers that were never issued.

sections.title: A Range of Early Network Topics
sections.content: The titles in the list cover many subjects, including host software, documentation, protocol proposals, meeting reports, network timing and interfaces. The list is an index only; it does not summarize the technical contents of each note.
sections.plainLanguage: The titles show that early notes covered both technical designs and coordination work. To learn what a note says, a reader needs to consult that note itself.

sections.title: How to Read the Entries
sections.content: Each entry pairs a note number and date with its NIC number, title and author information. The list is dated 23 December 1970 and is identified as NIC 5620.
sections.plainLanguage: Use the number, title or author to find an entry, then use its listed NIC number as a reference identifier. The catalog itself is dated December 1970.
